topic: The Flower: Symmetry, Whorls and Ovary Position
title: Reading a Flower Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A china rose, a pea flower and a small white guava flower each hide a secret: one splits evenly in many ways, one in just one way, and one hides its ovary below everything else. Diya asks how botanists describe a flower exactly.

You will see the parts and four whorls of a flower, cut flowers to find actinomorphic, zygomorphic and asymmetric symmetry, count trimerous to pentamerous parts and spot a bract, then watch one flower change from hypogynous to perigynous to epigynous as the thalamus rises around the ovary. Then hypogynous vs epigynous, a pause and think check, a worked example, the exam trap, an original NEET match the following question and a recap card.

This is Episode 44 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A china rose, a pea and a guava flower
0:31 Parts and the four whorls
1:15 Symmetry: one cut, many cuts or none
2:02 Where the ovary sits: hypo, peri, epi
2:44 Superior vs inferior ovary + pause and think
3:30 Worked example: read four flowers
3:56 Exam trap: what hypogynous means
4:19 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:44 Recap and three questions
